doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: The Owl Club, dance halls and the few trombonists who played for Giardina
summary: Places played in those days and the two trombonists, Edwards and Henry Brunies, who could play for Giardina.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Look at him. Well, the Owl Club was most of that colored place, wasn't it?
I don't know. I just read about it in a book, you know, and I wanted to find out what that was. Yeah, I want to play out.

It didn't register with me, you know. Yeah. The places we played in those days was the Lusitania, which is still on Leach and Field and Dauphine, I think. Yeah. And the Taunty Dancing School, which is out of existence for many years. And Millenburg, and I suppose. Who was out there
Jardina. Jardina? Jardina. Bacquet. Me, Tony. I know.
There was only two trombone players could play for Jardina.
Diddy Stevens used to play. Well,
Diddy Stevens played and they got me in the band.
There was only two trombone players.
One was named Eddie Edwards and the other was named Henry Brunas. and there must have been in those days another good seven or ten.
You know, that's the only folks could play with Jardina. Yeah, Georgie, Georgie, when I was playing with Lane in the parades, Georgie used to play Alto Horn with us. Jardina wouldn't
take a parade. He wouldn't march his men in a parade. Oh,
